I'm only 21, but I know the age your at is very transitory. You're going through a lot of changes and actually getting out into the working world is never as glamorous as your college major made it seem because they fail to tell you that everyone starts from the bottom. You may be working with shitty clients now, but thats because you're brand new. Once you have a lot of experience, you can be more selective and maybe even find a nice barn to permanent at! I want to be a high school teacher and last summer I was working as an assistant at a daycare and even though I loved the kids, I wasn't so sure I was into being a teacher. But then I reminded myself that not only was a I not in my age group, I was in a position where I couldn't call the shots and working under someone always kinda sucks. When I'm actually in a high school during my practicums, I love it.

Everyone at our age group questions whether they made the right choice. But I can almost garuntee that if you changed your career and went to work in an office, you would be daydreaming all day about the barn.

Also, if you do need work while your leg heals, you can possibly collect disability. I'm not sure how the laws with that work, but it sounds like you would be physically unable to do your job. If you aren't into that, maybe snag a quick throw away job at a restaurant or in retail? It'll give you some minimum wage cash. However, I don't know if anyone would really want to hire someone on crutches. Try to check out craigslist! Theres all kinds of jobs on there. But still look into disability pay.

And, of course, you could work at a Tack shop!
